chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Learning to shimmy in front of her mother's armoire
summary: Lu's mother taught her to sing and shimmy facing mirrors on the armoire, and the church choir doubted she was a professional singer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: What do you think your mother... You used to tell me about your mother taught you some of them steps at first, when you was a little girl?
My mother... We had one of these great big armoires, you know, with the two mirrors. She'd get on one side and I'd get on the other side, see. And...
What did you call them? A big what?

But it had a mirror on each side. See, so she'd get on one side and I'd get on the other. And we'd sing, you see. And we'd get in the mirror, and then she would show me how to shimmy, you know, and what to do. And I was singing the Blues...
You said when you got in the church and you did that, and the folks would say...

In the church, in the choir they asked me what I did, and I told them that I was an entertainer, I was a professional singer. And they would look at me like I was a fool. Because I couldn't learn a hymn!
